# visualization.design_map.correlation_map { #fmrimod.visualization.design_map.correlation_map }

```python
correlation_map(
    model,
    rotate_x_text=True,
    figsize=None,
    cmap='RdBu_r',
    annot=False,
    fmt='.2f',
    **kwargs,
)
```

Visualize correlation matrix of design matrix regressors.

Creates a heatmap showing the correlation between all pairs of
regressors in the design matrix.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type                        | Description                                                       | Default    |
|---------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| model         | EventModel or BaselineModel | Event model or baseline model containing the design matrix        | _required_ |
| rotate_x_text | bool                        | Whether to rotate x-axis labels                                   | `True`     |
| figsize       | tuple of float              | Figure size as (width, height). If None, automatically determined | `None`     |
| cmap          | str                         | Colormap name (diverging colormap recommended)                    | `'RdBu_r'` |
| annot         | bool                        | Whether to annotate cells with correlation values                 | `False`    |
| fmt           | str                         | Format string for annotations                                     | `'.2f'`    |
| **kwargs      | object                      | Additional arguments passed to seaborn's heatmap                  | `{}`       |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                     | Description       |
|--------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| fig    | matplotlib.figure.Figure | The figure object |
| ax     | matplotlib.axes.Axes     | The axes object   |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Basic correlation map
>>> fig, ax = correlation_map(model)
>>>
>>> # With correlation values shown
>>> fig, ax = correlation_map(model, annot=True, figsize=(10, 8))
```
